newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-MORGAN OPENS FIVE-STROKE LEAD AT THE TRADITION.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MORGAN OPENS FIVE-STROKE LEAD AT THE TRADITION.

text.p: Gil Morgan continued his record-setting play Saturday and opened a five-shot lead after three rounds of the $1.2 million Tradition, the Senior Tour's first major tournament of the year.

Morgan's 54-hole total of 17-under-par 199 is a tournament record, breaking the mark of 202 set in 1993 by Tom Shaw. Morgan began the day with a two-shot lead, but blistered the Cochise course for a 5-under 67 -- his third straight round in the 60s.
Told he set a 54-hole record, Morgan said: "Is it? Unbelievable."

John Jacobs and Japan's Isao Aoki carded 70s and were five shots behind Morgan. Terry Dill, who was tied with Jacobs and Aoki after the second round, shot a 71 for sole possession of fourth at 11-under 205.

Graham Marsh of Australia recorded his second straight 69 and was seven shots off the pace. Jim Dent shot 70 and was sixth at 9-under 207, followed by George Archer at 8-under and Bob Eastwood and Larry Gilbert at 7-under.

Morgan shed the red wool cap he wore during the first two rounds and started his third round slowly, bogeying the par-4 third hole. But he recovered quickly with a birdie at the fourth hole and made the turn at 13-under after another birdie at eight.
Morgan caught fire on the back nine, collecting four birdies to distance himself from the field.

"I haven't made very many mistakes, really," he said. "The ones that I've made, most of them I have been able to recover from. I have kept the ball in play pretty much. I don't think I've hit in the desert yet."

Leading at a major is nothing new for Morgan, although bringing a lead into Sunday is. He had a four-shot lead at the 1976 PGA Championship and led midway through the 1984 Masters before tying for third.
"I want to just go play (Sunday) and see what happens," Morgan said.

"I'm sure I'll be a little nervous playing here, this being my first major and being this out in front. But I will try to control it, try to play my game as much as possible, try to hit the fairways and greens and try not to make too many mistakes.
"I hope I can hit it close to the hole and make a few putts."
The 50-year-old Morgan joined the Senior Tour last September and won the Ralphs Senior Classic one week later. He is still looking for his first win this year, but is fifth on the 1997 money list.
Defending champion Jack Nicklaus, a four-time winner of this event and designer of the Cochise course on which it is played, posted a 3-over 75 and was 17 shots back at even-par 216.

He was not the only big name out of contention. A 3-under 69 lifted Hale Irwin to 4-under 212, one stroke better than 1994 champion Ray Floyd. Lee Trevino, who won here in 1992, was at 3-over 219, while two-time Senior Tour Player of the Year Jim Colbert was a whopping 24 shots back at 7-over 223.
David Graham, the 1997 money leader, posted a 71 and was at 1-over 217. He was coming off a one-shot victory at last week's Dominion.

"A lot of weird guys up here on the leaderboard," Morgan said. "We're all pretty weird. You expect Raymond to do well and you expect Hale to do well and Jack and Colbert and the guys that have done well over the last couple of years. Sometimes it just doesn't happen. Maybe the major championship has got them. I don't know."

Dill's 71 included a par at the 15th hole, where he popped up his tee shot and dropped his ball into the backyard pool of a house adjoining the fairway. Because the course has no out of bounds, Dill was allowed to drop his ball without penalty, hit a wedge and ended up missing a birdie putt.
"I was really lucky there," he said. "That was something, to be on national television in the swimming pool, which was part of the course. It was funny."
